newsitem.title: UK: Bosnia talks link aid to peace, war criminals.
newsitem.headline: Bosnia talks link aid to peace, war criminals.

text.p: Major powers were set to end a two-day peace conference on Thursday by telling Bosnia's ethnic leaders they must fully implement a year-old peace pact and issue arrest warrants for war criminals or forfeit Western aid.

"The council's willingness to devote human and financial resources is dependent on a strengthened commitment from the authorities in Bosnia-Herzegovina to implementation of the peace agreement," according to a draft document obtained by Reuters.
The conference, attended by more than 50 nations, was also set to tell the leaders of the former Yugoslavia they must round up indicted war criminals if they wanted more help.

The provisions of the draft London document ensure that "the authorities concerned execute arrest warrants against indictees and surrender them to the (Hague war crimes) tribunal without further delay."
The conference was called to assess the state of peace one year after the fighting stopped.
Frustration over repeated delays in implementing the civilian aspects of the so-called Dayton agreement has led Western leaders to link aid to a renewed commitment to genuine peace on the ground.
